title: Training Questions and Answers: Seasonal Comparison in Electricity Estimates
content:
# Seasonal Comparison in Electricity Estimates — Utility Services Program

**Rule.** On a Utility Services Program account, the recent electricity average of an estimated electricity line is adjusted for season by last year's electricity read of the same service month — the actual electricity read dated at least twelve and fewer than thirteen whole months before the billing date:

- when that read exists and at least 12 actual electricity reads are dated fewer than thirteen whole months before the billing date, the seasonal estimate is the mean of the recent electricity average and last year's read;
- when that read exists and fewer than 12 actual electricity reads are dated in those thirteen months, the seasonal estimate is last year's read;
- in every other situation the seasonal estimate is the recent electricity average.

Each is rounded to 3 decimals.

## Questions answered

**What is "last year's read of the same service month"?** The actual electricity read dated at least twelve and fewer than thirteen whole months before the billing date. An estimated read in that band does not count.

**What does "at least 12 actual reads in thirteen months" count?** Every actual electricity read on the account dated fewer than thirteen whole months before the billing date, last year's read included.

**What if there is no actual read twelve to thirteen months back?** Then the seasonal estimate is the recent electricity average, whatever the number of other reads.

## Cases (hypothetical kWh)

| Last year's read | Actual reads in thirteen months | Recent electricity average | Seasonal estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 720.00 | 12 | 600.000 | 660.000 (mean of 600.000 and 720.00) |
| 720.00 | 8 | 600.000 | 720.000 |
| none | 11 | 600.000 | 600.000 |
